text:
Hi Professor Alvarez,

I'd like to book our 30-minute 1:1 for next week. Looking at my calendar, I have these free half-hours inside working hours:

- Monday 10:00-10:30
- Monday 14:00-14:30
- Thursday 10:00-10:30
- Thursday 14:00-14:30
- Friday 11:00-11:30

Which of these works for you? Happy to take another slot if none of them do.

Best,
John
Good morning, Professor Alvarez — I'd like to book my 30-minute 1:1 for next week. Would Monday 10:00-10:30 work for you? If not, I'm also free Tuesday 11:00-11:30 or Friday 11:00-11:30.

Hi Professor Alvarez — I'd like to set up our 30-minute 1:1 for next week. Would Monday 10:00–10:30 work for you? If that's taken, I'm also free Monday 14:00–14:30. Let me know which suits you and I'll put it on my calendar.

Thanks,
Sarah

Hi Sarah — Monday 10:00–10:30 works for me. Booked it. See you then, and I'll have a look at your latest draft beforehand.

— Professor Alvarez

Hi John — Monday 14:00–14:30 is free on my side, so let's take that one. Booked. (Monday 10:00–10:30 just went to Sarah, and Thursday 14:00–14:30 / Friday 11:00–11:30 collide with my committees and paper review.)

— Professor Alvarez

Good morning, Priya — Monday 10:00–10:30 is taken (Sarah has it), so let's do Tuesday 11:00–11:30. Booked it. Please bring the experiment results.

— Professor Alvarez

Hello — for the official schedule: I've booked my student 1:1s next week as Monday 10:00–10:30 (Sarah), Monday 14:00–14:30 (John) and Tuesday 11:00–11:30 (Priya). Please let me know if any of those clash with department lectures, seminars or university meetings.

— Professor Alvarez

Hello Professor Alvarez — checked against next week's official schedule:

- Mon 10:00–10:30 (Sarah): no clash.
- Mon 14:00–14:30 (John): no clash.
- Tue 11:00–11:30 (Priya): clashes — Seminar runs Tue 09:50–11:10, so it overlaps your slot by ten minutes.

So only the Tuesday one needs moving.

Perfect, thank you — it's on my calendar for Monday 10:00–10:30. I'll bring the latest draft so we can go through it together. See you then.

— Sarah
Perfect — Tuesday 11:00–11:30 it is, and it's in my calendar. I'll bring the experiment results.

Great — Monday 14:00–14:30 works for me. I've put it in my calendar. See you then.

John

Thanks for checking. Two other half-hours look open on my side — could you tell me whether either clashes with the official schedule: Wednesday 10:00–10:30 and Thursday 10:00–10:30? I'll move Priya to whichever is clear.

Priya — small snag: Tuesday 11:00–11:30 overlaps the department seminar (09:50–11:10), so I need to move us. Friday 11:00–11:30 is out for me (paper review runs to 11:30). Could you do Wednesday 10:00–10:30 or Thursday 10:00–10:30? Tell me which and I'll lock it in — I'm confirming those slots with the department office in parallel.

— Professor Alvarez

Checked:

- Wed 10:00–10:30: clashes — CSE455 office hours run Wed 10:00–11:30.
- Thu 10:00–10:30: clear. The Thursday items nearby end at 10:00 (Guest lecture prep, Seminar) and the next ones start at 10:30 (Department seminar, CSE444 lecture).

So Thursday 10:00–10:30 works.
Perfect — I'll take Thursday 10:00–10:30 for Priya and drop the Tuesday slot. No further changes. Thanks for the quick check.

Priya — the department came back: Thursday 10:00–10:30 is clear (Wed 10:00–10:30 clashes with my office hours), so please move us to Thursday 10:00–10:30 and drop Tuesday 11:00–11:30. Sorry for the shuffle — the seminar runs Tue 09:50–11:10. See you Thursday.

— Professor Alvarez

Hello — Priya here. Professor Alvarez mentioned a department seminar 09:50–11:10 on Tuesday next week, but my schedule has CSE444 lecture 09:00–10:30 and CSE452 lecture 10:30–11:00 at that time. Could you confirm the official schedule for next week, and whether Wednesday 10:00–10:30 and Thursday 10:00–10:30 are free of official commitments? I'd also like to avoid double-booking my 1:1 with the professor while you two are confirming slots.

Hello Priya — yes, those three Tuesday items are all on the official schedule for next week: CSE444 lecture Tue 09:00–10:30, Seminar Tue 09:50–11:10, CSE452 lecture Tue 10:30–11:00. So the seminar does overlap both lectures.

On your two half-hours:
- Wed 10:00–10:30: not free — CSE455 office hours run Wed 10:00–11:30.
- Thu 10:00–10:30: free of official commitments (Thursday items end at 10:00 and resume at 10:30).

I don't keep or discuss anyone's private appointments, so please confirm your 1:1 slot directly with Professor Alvarez.

Confirmed: Thursday 10:00–10:30 it is — Tuesday 11:00–11:30 is dropped and Thursday is in my calendar. The department confirms Thu 10:00–10:30 is free of official commitments (and that Wed 10:00–10:30 clashes with your office hours). One thing: my calendar still shows Reading group Thu 09:50–11:10, which would overlap the first ten minutes — has that moved to 10:30, or should I slip in at 10:10? Either way I'll be there with the experiment results.

Priya — the department's official schedule has nothing between 10:00 and 10:30 (Guest lecture prep and Seminar end at 10:00; Department seminar starts at 10:30), and the reading group isn't on the official list, so I can't confirm it moved. My slot stays Thursday 10:00–10:30.

Plan: come at 10:00 and we finish sharp at 10:30 — I have the department seminar right after. If the reading group really runs to 11:10, step out at 10:00 (or check whether it has moved yourself); 10:10 would only leave us twenty minutes and would push me into the seminar. See you Thursday with the results.

— Professor Alvarez
Understood — Thursday 10:00 sharp, finishing at 10:30, and I'll step out of reading group (I'm checking with Sarah and John whether it has moved). I'll bring the experiment results.
